theory1.instructions: Answer all 45 questions. Each question has one best answer: choose it. Each question is worth 1 mark. Time allowed: 2 hours 30 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

questions.stem: What is planned preventive maintenance?
options: Repairing equipment only after it has broken down
Servicing equipment at set intervals to stop failures
Replacing all equipment every year, worn or not
Letting the operators fix things whenever they have time

questions.stem: A plant measures motor vibration and insulation resistance every month, and plans repairs when the readings change. What is this called?
options: Breakdown maintenance carried out after each failure
Run-to-failure maintenance with no checks in between
Emergency maintenance done on the night shift
Condition-based maintenance

questions.stem: Why does a maintenance department keep an asset register of its electrical equipment?
options: So each item's location, details and history are known
So the equipment can be sold off quickly when it is old
So the operators know whose turn it is to do the cleaning
So the power company can bill each machine separately

questions.stem: Where should the maintenance tasks and intervals for a newly installed UPS come from first?
options: From whatever was done on an older UPS in the building
From the electrician's memory of other similar jobs
From the maker's operation and maintenance manual
From the cleaning staff's weekly checklist

questions.stem: A motor's bearings must be greased every 2 000 running hours. It runs 16 hours a day, 5 days a week. About how many weeks is that?
options: 20 weeks
40 weeks
25 weeks
12 weeks

questions.stem: Why must a motor bearing be greased with the type and amount of grease the maker gives, not 'as much as it will take'?
options: Too much can overheat the bearing and reach the windings
Extra grease makes the motor turn the wrong way when it starts
Extra grease stops the overload relay from tripping
The maker only sells its grease in very small tins

questions.stem: A motor's insulation resistance, measured once a year in the same conditions, reads 200 MΩ, 150 MΩ, 60 MΩ and then 15 MΩ. What should you do?
options: Nothing, because 15 MΩ is still a reading
Stop taking the readings, as they are confusing
Raise the test voltage so that it reads higher
Plan cleaning, drying or repair before it fails

questions.stem: During planned maintenance of a distribution board, which task is done with it isolated and proved dead?
options: Thermal imaging of the joints while the board is loaded
Checking terminal torque and cleaning out dust
Measuring the running current of each circuit
Pressing each GFCI's test button to see it trip

questions.stem: Why is thermal imaging of a board done by the authorised person while the board is carrying its normal load?
options: Loose joints only heat up when current flows
The camera will not work on a cold board at all
It is quicker than switching the board off
The camera needs the panel lights on to see

questions.stem: During maintenance, a contactor's main contacts are found badly pitted and burnt. What is the correct action?
options: File them smooth with a flat file and refit them
Bend the contacts so that they press together harder
Replace the contacts or contactor as the maker says
Put grease on them so that they close more smoothly

questions.stem: Lead-acid batteries for a standby system are kept in a small room. Why must the room be ventilated?
options: To keep the batteries cool enough that they never wear out
Charging gives off hydrogen, which can explode
To stop anyone from stealing the batteries at night
So the acid in the batteries can evaporate faster

questions.stem: A 12 V, 100 Ah battery feeds a 10 A load. Ignoring losses, about how long could it run?
options: 1 hour
100 hours
1.2 hours
10 hours

questions.stem: Which PPE is needed when handling or topping up wet lead-acid batteries?
options: A dust mask and a pair of cotton gloves only
Ear defenders and a hard hat, and nothing else
A welding helmet and a leather welding apron
Goggles or face shield, acid-proof gloves and apron

questions.stem: Why are emergency lights given a full-duration test at set intervals, as well as short monthly checks?
options: To use up old batteries so that they can be thrown away
To prove the batteries still last the rated time
To check that the lamps give the right colour of light
To reset the clocks inside the emergency fittings

questions.stem: When is the best time to carry out a full-duration emergency lighting test in a hotel?
options: On a busy evening, so the guests can see it working
Just before a fire drill, so that the batteries are already flat
At a quiet time, as the batteries need hours to recharge
Late at night, when the main lights must be off anyway

questions.stem: A pump control panel will be fixed outdoors under a roof edge at a hotel in Port Antonio, where wind drives the rain. What should you check first?
options: That its IP rating suits wind-driven rain and dust
That it is painted to match the hotel's colours
That its door opens to the left rather than the right
That it is the cheapest panel the supplier stocks

questions.stem: A UPS and its battery cabinet are installed in a store room. Why must the maker's clearances around them be kept?
options: So that the cleaner can sweep behind the cabinets
So air can cool them and they can be serviced
So the cabinets look neat, standing in a straight line
So that the floor under them need not be level

questions.stem: A 40 kg transformer is to be mounted on a hollow block wall. What should you check before fixing it?
options: That the fixings are rated for that load in that wall
That the wall has been painted at some time within the last year
That the transformer's label will face upwards
That the fixings are the same colour as the wall

questions.stem: A cable enters an outdoor enclosure from below through a gland. Why are the correct gland size and seal important?
options: So that the cable can be pulled out easily later on
So the enclosure can be opened without any tools
So that the cable is earthed through the rubber seal
So water, dust and insects cannot get in

questions.stem: A panel at a farm in St. Elizabeth has ants and a lizard nest inside, with burn marks on a terminal. After it is isolated and cleaned, what should be done?
options: Spray insecticide inside the panel every week while it is live
Leave the panel door open so that the insects can get out
Seal unused entries and gaps, and repair the damage
Fill the whole panel with expanding foam to block them

questions.stem: Why do switchgear and fittings near the coast in Jamaica need more frequent inspection?
options: Sea air makes the supply voltage rise during the day
The power company asks for it at all coastal sites
Salt air speeds up corrosion of metal parts and joints
Buildings near the coast use more electricity

questions.stem: Why does a maintenance team keep critical spares, such as a pump's contactor and capacitor, in stock?
options: So that they can be sold on to other companies
So the store looks full when the auditor visits
So that old parts can be thrown away sooner
So a breakdown can be fixed without long waits

questions.stem: Before routine maintenance inside a motor control centre, what must be done first?
options: Isolate, lock off, tag and prove dead the section
Switch off the lights in the room for safety
Tell the operators to slow their machines down for the morning
Open all the doors to let the heat out first

questions.stem: Only one section of a large switchboard can be isolated for maintenance. What should be done about the live sections nearby?
options: Work quickly near them and keep one hand in a pocket
Fit barriers or shrouds and mark the live parts
Take their covers off so they can be seen clearly
Spray them with water to keep them cool

questions.stem: Why is every maintenance task recorded with its date, readings and the name of the person who did it?
options: To show trends and prove the work was done
So that the worker can be paid twice for it
So that the job can be skipped next time round
So the maker will send new equipment free

questions.stem: A warehouse has 120 LED high-bay fittings. Why might the client plan to clean them as a group, at set intervals?
options: So that the fittings change colour more slowly over time
Dust on the fittings cuts the light reaching the floor
So that the fittings use more energy and stay warm
Because LED fittings must be opened up every month

questions.stem: A restaurant's kitchen extract fan is on the maintenance schedule. What electrical risk does grease build-up add?
options: It makes the fan run faster and more quietly
It improves the earth connection of the fan
It can overheat the motor and is a fire risk
It lowers the amount of power the fan uses

questions.stem: A standby generator is started and run on load at set intervals by the authorised person. Why?
options: To use up old fuel so that new fuel can go in
So the neighbours can hear that it is working
So the battery charger can be switched off for good
To prove it will start and take the load when needed

questions.stem: A new machine's nameplate says 380–415 V three-phase. The building has only a 110/220 V single-phase supply. What should you do?
options: Connect it to 220 V, as it will just run a little slower
Connect it across two 110 V circuits to make up 220 V
Fit a bigger breaker so that it can draw more current
Stop, and advise on a suitable supply or another machine

questions.stem: Which documents should be handed over with newly installed electrical equipment?
options: The packing boxes and the delivery note only
A photograph of the team who installed it
Test results, the maker's manual and a maintenance schedule
The installer's own list of personal tools

questions.stem: During planned maintenance, terminals are checked with a torque screwdriver. Why not just tighten them all as hard as possible?
options: Hard tightening makes the circuit draw more current than before
Over-tightening can damage the terminal or conductor
Very tight screws stop the breaker from tripping
The maker wants the screws left slightly loose

questions.stem: A water heater's local isolator is to be fitted in a bathroom. Where should it be placed?
options: Out of reach of the shower spray, as the rules and maker say
Inside the shower area, so that it is easy to reach
Low down on the floor, underneath the heater
Behind the heater, where it is out of sight

questions.stem: How often should the test button on a GFCI (RCD) be pressed by the user?
options: Never, because pressing it wears the device out
At the interval shown on the maker's label
Only when it has already tripped by itself
Every day before the supply is used

questions.stem: Maintenance of a hotel's main switchboard needs the supply off. When is the best time?
options: At check-in time on a busy Saturday afternoon
In the middle of the busiest week of the year
Without notice, so that the guests are not worried
At an agreed quiet time, with guests and staff told

questions.stem: Before maintenance work in a roof space above a classroom, what should your risk assessment cover?
options: The colour of the ceiling tiles below the roof
Which trainee will sweep up after the work
Heat, access, fragile ceilings, cables and lighting
The date of the next school holiday

questions.stem: You supervise two trainees doing the monthly checks on 30 emergency lights. How do you make sure the checks are done properly?
options: Give a checklist, show the first ones, then spot-check
Let them sign off all 30 lights together at the end of the day
Do every check yourself while the trainees watch
Ask the hotel staff whether the lights look all right

questions.stem: A new extract fan is to be installed in a factory wall. Which check comes before the cable is run?
options: That the fan blades have been painted
That the fan's box is kept in case of return
That circuit, isolator and fixings suit the fan's data
That the fan is the quietest model on the market

questions.stem: During maintenance, the PVC cable to an outdoor pump is found cracked and brittle from the sun. What is the right action?
options: Replace it with sun-resistant cable, or protect it in conduit
Paint the cable to cover up the cracks
Wrap the cracked parts in tape and leave it
Wipe it with oil to soften it again

questions.stem: Why must new equipment and its isolator be labelled when they are installed?
options: So that the equipment is easier to sell when it is replaced later
So anyone can identify it and isolate the right supply
So that the maker can trace who bought the item
So that the equipment looks finished and tidy

questions.stem: A machine broke down three times in a month, each time from a loose cable connection. What change to the maintenance plan makes most sense?
options: Stop maintaining the machine, as it keeps failing anyway
Wait for a fourth breakdown, and then decide what to do
Replace the whole machine with a new one straight away
Add connection checks and find out why they loosen

questions.stem: A 2 kW heater runs 5 hours a day for 30 days. The assessor gives the electricity price as J$60 per kWh. What is the cost?
A 220/24 V control transformer is found very hot during maintenance checks. Which is the most likely cause?
options: The 24 V side has too few loads connected to it
The supply to the transformer is at 50 Hz
The transformer case is painted a dark colour
It is overloaded beyond its VA rating

questions.stem: About how much current can a 100 VA, 24 V control transformer supply at 24 V?
What should be done with old lead-acid batteries removed from a UPS?
options: Put them in the general waste skip
Bury them well away from the building
Send them to an approved battery recycler
Empty them down a drain, then bin them

questions.stem: After maintenance on a client's equipment, what should be left with the client?
options: Nothing at all, if nothing was found wrong
A record of the checks, readings, faults and advice
The old grease, rags and used cable ties
A blank form for the client to fill in

theory2.instructions: Section A has 15 short answers (2 marks each). Section B has 10 essay questions (5 marks each): answer each in full sentences. Time allowed: 3 hours 35 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

shortAnswers.stem: A 12 V, 200 Ah battery feeds a 20 A load. Ignoring losses, about how many hours could it run?
A motor's bearings need greasing every 1 500 running hours. It runs 10 hours a day, 6 days a week. How many weeks is that?
Which gas, given off when lead-acid batteries are charged, can explode?
In an 'O&M manual', what do the letters O and M stand for?
What name is given to maintenance that is done only after equipment has failed?
A 3 kW water heater runs 4 hours a day. How many kilowatt-hours does it use in 30 days?
A control transformer is rated 250 VA at 24 V. What is its full-load current in amps, to one decimal place?
What is the name of the list of all the equipment a maintenance team looks after, with its location and details?
What word is used for a planned stop of equipment, agreed in advance, so that maintenance can be done?
What is the name of the test in which emergency lights run on battery for their full rated time?
In what unit is a battery's capacity given?
What word describes the small craters burnt into a contactor's contacts by arcing?
What is the name of the list of faults to be put right after an inspection or installation?
In what unit is a torque screwdriver set?
What do the letters CMMS stand for, the computer system used to plan maintenance and keep its records?

essays.stem: A 60-room hotel in Ocho Rios asks you to set up a planned maintenance programme for its electrical equipment. Explain how you would do it.
essays.modelAnswer: I would start by surveying the hotel and building an asset register: every board, motor, pump, water heater, air conditioner, emergency light, generator, UPS and lighting area, with its location, rating and age. I would collect the makers' manuals and any past records. Then I would rank each item by how critical it is: the main switchboard, generator, water pumps and emergency lights matter most for safety and guests. For each item I would set the tasks and intervals from the maker's manual, adjusted for the coast's salt air, heat and humidity. Tasks would include inspections, cleaning, torque checks, insulation resistance tests, battery checks, emergency light tests and generator runs. I would plan safe isolation and outages at quiet times, and list the spares to keep. Each task would have a checklist and a record, kept in a logbook or a computer system. I would review the programme every year using the records and any breakdowns.
markingPoints: Builds an asset register by survey with makers' manuals
Ranks items by how critical they are
Sets tasks and intervals from the manuals, adjusted for local conditions
Plans safe isolation, outages and spares
Uses checklists and records, and reviews the programme

essays.stem: Compare breakdown maintenance, planned preventive maintenance and condition-based maintenance. Give an example of where each would be a sensible choice.
essays.modelAnswer: Breakdown maintenance means repairing an item only when it fails. It costs nothing until then, but failures come without warning and can stop work. It suits cheap, non-critical items where failure is harmless, such as a lamp in a store room. Planned preventive maintenance means servicing at set intervals, by time or running hours, such as greasing bearings every 2 000 hours or testing emergency lights each month. It reduces surprise failures but may replace parts that still had life. It suits items where failure is serious and wear is predictable, such as a hotel's water pumps or emergency lighting. Condition-based maintenance means measuring the condition, such as insulation resistance, vibration or temperature, and acting when readings change. It avoids unnecessary work and catches problems early, but needs instruments, skill and records. It suits large, costly or critical motors and switchboards, such as the main pumps at a factory. Most sites use a mix of all three.
markingPoints: Explains breakdown maintenance with a suitable example
Explains planned preventive maintenance with a suitable example
Explains condition-based maintenance with a suitable example
Gives advantages and drawbacks of each
Says that a mix is usually used

essays.stem: Describe how you would plan and carry out annual maintenance on a factory's motor control centre, including which checks are done live by the authorised person and which are done dead.
essays.modelAnswer: I would read the maker's manual and last year's records, then agree a shutdown time with production and arrange a permit. Before the shutdown, while the board is on normal load, the authorised person scans it with a thermal imaging camera and records running currents, so hot joints and overloaded circuits can be found. I would not do these live checks as a trainee. At the shutdown, the board is isolated at its supply, locked off, tagged and proved dead with a tester checked before and after, with barriers on anything that stays live. Then the team does the dead work: vacuum out dust, inspect for heat marks, corrosion and insect damage, check every terminal to the maker's torque, check contactor contacts and replace worn ones, check that overload settings match the motors, and test insulation resistance of the motor circuits. Hot spots found on the scan are remade. After the work, dead tests are done, the authorised person restores the supply and checks operation, and all readings are recorded and compared with last year's.
markingPoints: Uses the manual and past records, and agrees the shutdown and permit
Live checks (thermal imaging, currents) done only by the authorised person under load
Isolates, locks off, tags and proves dead, with barriers on live parts
Dead tasks: cleaning, inspection, torque, contacts, overload settings, insulation tests; repairs hot spots
Dead tests, supply restored by the authorised person, readings recorded and compared

essays.stem: A medical clinic in Kingston is having a UPS with a lead-acid battery cabinet installed to keep its computers and equipment running. Explain what you would consider when installing it, and what its maintenance plan should include.
essays.modelAnswer: I would read the maker's installation manual first. The UPS needs a dry, cool, ventilated room, because heat shortens battery life and charging gives off hydrogen. The floor must carry the weight of the batteries, and the maker's clearances must be kept for cooling and service. The supply cable and protective devices are sized from the maker's data, with a lockable isolator, and the output circuits are clearly labelled so staff know what is on the UPS. A bypass switch lets the UPS be maintained without losing supply. The earthing must follow the maker's instructions. After dead tests, the authorised person commissions it and checks the run time on battery. The maintenance plan should include regular checks of alarms and the display, keeping the room cool and clean, checking battery terminals for corrosion and tightness with the system isolated as the maker says, periodic battery tests, and replacing batteries at the end of their life. Records of every check are kept.
markingPoints: Location: dry, cool, ventilated, strong floor, maker's clearances
Supply sized from maker's data with isolator, labelled outputs, bypass and correct earthing
Dead tests and commissioning by the authorised person, including run time
Maintenance: alarms, temperature, cleanliness, terminals checked as the maker says, battery tests and replacement
Keeps records

essays.stem: Explain the hazards of working with lead-acid batteries for standby systems, and the precautions you would take during their maintenance.
essays.modelAnswer: Lead-acid batteries hold a lot of energy and cannot be switched off, so a short circuit across the terminals with a spanner can cause a flash, burns and molten metal. Charging gives off hydrogen, which can explode if a spark or flame is near. The acid is corrosive and burns the skin and eyes. Batteries are heavy and can injure backs and feet. To work safely I would follow the maker's instructions and the site's rules: keep the battery room ventilated and free of flames and smoking, use insulated tools, take off rings and watches, and isolate the charger and the load before disconnecting anything. I would wear goggles or a face shield, acid-resistant gloves and an apron, and make sure an eyewash station and water are close by. Batteries are lifted with help or a trolley. Spilt acid is neutralised and cleaned as the SDS says. Old batteries go to an approved recycler, and all checks are recorded.
markingPoints: Explains short-circuit and burn hazard
Explains hydrogen explosion risk and the need for ventilation and no ignition sources
Explains acid hazard and the PPE and eyewash needed
Uses insulated tools, removes jewellery and isolates charger and load
Safe lifting, spill handling by the SDS, recycling and records

essays.stem: Describe a maintenance routine for the emergency lighting in a three-storey hotel, and explain why each part of it matters.
essays.modelAnswer: I would follow the maker's instructions and the specification for the intervals. Usually there is a short monthly function test: each emergency light is switched to battery, often with a test key switch, to check that it lights, then returned to normal. This shows that the lamp, battery and changeover work. At longer intervals, often once a year, there is a full-duration test, where the lights run on battery for their full rated time. This proves the batteries still hold enough charge to light escape routes for the whole time needed. The full test is done at a quiet time, because the batteries take many hours to recharge and the building is less protected until they do. Each fitting's charging indicator is checked, and lenses are cleaned. Any light that fails is recorded and repaired or its battery replaced quickly. All results go in a logbook, which the fire officer or insurer may ask to see.
markingPoints: Monthly short function test and why it matters
Periodic full-duration test and why it matters
Full test at a quiet time because of recharge time
Checks indicators, cleans lenses, repairs failures promptly
Records results in a logbook for inspection

essays.stem: A pump motor's yearly insulation resistance readings, taken at the same test voltage, are: 300 MΩ, 280 MΩ, 90 MΩ and now 12 MΩ. Explain what this trend tells you and describe a maintenance plan for the motor.
essays.modelAnswer: The first two readings are high and steady, which shows good insulation. Then the reading drops sharply to 90 MΩ and then to 12 MΩ. Even if 12 MΩ is still above a minimum value, the fast fall shows that the insulation is getting worse, probably from moisture, dirt, oil or heat damage. If nothing is done, it may soon fail, trip the protection or become unsafe. I would plan to isolate, lock off and prove dead the motor, then inspect the terminal box and windings for water, dust and damage, and check the gland and seals. I would clean it and dry it by an approved method as the maker says, then retest and compare. If the reading does not recover, I would recommend a rewind or replacement before it fails, at a planned time. I would also check the bearings, vibration and connections, record all results, and test more often until the trend is steady.
markingPoints: Explains that early readings show good insulation
Explains that the sharp fall shows deterioration even if above a minimum
Gives likely causes (moisture, dirt, oil, heat)
Plan: isolate, inspect, clean and dry by the maker's method, retest; rewind or replace if not recovered
Checks other items, records and increases test frequency

essays.stem: Explain how Jamaica's climate and conditions affect the installation and maintenance of electrical equipment, and what you would do about each.
essays.modelAnswer: Heat makes equipment run hotter and shortens the life of batteries, capacitors and electronics, so I would keep ventilation and clearances, avoid placing panels in full sun, and check temperatures during maintenance. High humidity and rain bring moisture into enclosures and motors, so I would choose enclosures with a suitable IP rating, use proper glands and seals, and test insulation resistance regularly. Salt air near the coast corrodes metal, so I would use corrosion-resistant materials, protect joints and inspect more often. Strong sun cracks PVC cables and plastic, so I would use sun-resistant cables or conduit. Insects, lizards and rodents get into panels, so unused entries are sealed and panels inspected and cleaned. Lightning and storms cause surges, so surge protection and good earthing are needed and checked. Hurricanes bring flooding and wind damage, so equipment is mounted above flood levels where possible, fixed firmly, and checked and dried before re-energising after a storm.
markingPoints: Heat: ventilation, clearances, shade, temperature checks
Humidity and rain: IP rating, glands, insulation tests
Salt air and sun: corrosion-resistant materials, sun-resistant cables, more frequent inspection
Pests: sealing entries, cleaning
Lightning and hurricanes: surge protection, earthing, mounting height, checks after storms

essays.stem: A car park in Montego Bay needs its outdoor lights controlled by a new panel with a contactor, a time switch and a photocell. Describe how you would install and commission the panel.
essays.modelAnswer: I would check the drawing, the lighting load and the makers' data, and choose a contactor rated for the lighting load, a time switch and a photocell suited to outdoor use. The panel must have an IP rating suitable for wind-driven rain and salt air, with corrosion-resistant fixings, and be mounted where it is reachable, out of flood water and not in the way of vehicles. The photocell is placed where it sees daylight but not the car park lights. With the supply circuit isolated, locked off, tagged and proved dead, I would mount the panel, bring cables in through correctly sized glands from below, fit a lockable isolator, and wire it to the drawing with labelled wires. I would earth the panel and label it. Then I would do dead tests: continuity of protective conductors, insulation resistance and polarity. The authorised person energises it, sets the time switch and checks that the photocell and time switch control the contactor. I would hand over the drawing, settings, test results and a maintenance schedule.
markingPoints: Selects parts rated for the load and outdoor use; suitable IP rating and location
Places the photocell correctly
Isolates and proves dead; installs with correct glands, isolator, wiring, earthing and labels
Carries out dead tests; authorised person energises, sets and tests the controls
Hands over drawing, settings, test results and maintenance schedule

essays.stem: After a maintenance visit to a guest house, you found several problems of different urgency. Explain how you would write your maintenance report and present it to the owner.
essays.modelAnswer: I would write a short, clear report with the date, the site, the equipment checked and who did the work. For each item, I would give what was checked, the readings, and whether it passed. I would list the problems in order of priority. Urgent items are those that are dangerous now, such as a damaged cable or a missing earth, which I would make safe on the day and report straight away. Items to fix soon are those that will fail or become unsafe, such as worn contactor contacts or a falling insulation reading. Items to watch are those that are fine but changing. For each, I would give a recommended action and an estimated cost in J$, with GCT at the current rate where it applies. I would attach photos. I would go through the report with the owner in plain words, answer questions, and agree what will be done and when, then file a copy in the maintenance records.
markingPoints: Includes date, site, equipment, readings and who did the work
Sorts problems by priority (urgent, soon, watch)
Makes urgent dangers safe immediately
Gives actions and costs in J$ with GCT at the current rate, with photos
Explains it to the owner in plain words, agrees actions and files the record

practical1.title: Carry out planned maintenance on a training distribution board and motor starter, and report the findings
practical1.brief: The assessor gives the group the maker's data, a maintenance checklist and last year's readings for a training distribution board and a motor starter with its motor. Before the task, the instructor records the running currents and, if the Centre has a thermal camera, takes a thermal image of the board on load, and gives the group these results. As a group: (1) plan the job: tasks, order, who leads each, the isolation and a short risk assessment; (2) isolate the board and starter, every member fits a personal lock to a hasp, and the leader proves dead with a tester checked on a proving unit before and after; (3) clean out dust, and inspect for heat marks, corrosion, insects and damage; (4) check every terminal with a torque screwdriver to the maker's value and record any that were loose; (5) inspect the contactor contacts and the overload setting against the motor nameplate; (6) test insulation resistance of the motor circuit and the board's circuits (electronics disconnected) and compare with last year's readings; (7) put right what the assessor allows, and record the rest; (8) the instructor restores the supply and checks operation while the group stands clear; and (9) write a maintenance report with readings, trends, problems sorted by priority and recommended actions. Each member leads one task and records its results. Photograph each stage and hand in the plan, checklist and report.
materials: Training distribution board and motor starter with motor (switched only by the instructor)
Maker's data, maintenance checklist and last year's readings from the assessor
Instructor's running current readings and thermal image, if available
Two-pole voltage tester and proving unit, hasp, lock and tag for each member
Torque screwdriver, screwdrivers, soft brush and vacuum cleaner
Insulation resistance tester and low-resistance ohmmeter
Spare contactor contacts or a spare contactor, if the assessor allows
photos: The job plan and risk assessment
The hasp with every member's lock, and proving dead
The board and starter before cleaning, showing any findings
Terminals being checked with the torque screwdriver
Contactor contacts and the overload setting
Insulation resistance tests, and the readings compared with last year's
checklist: Planned the work and isolation clearly
Fitted their own lock and followed safe isolation, proving dead with the tester checked before and after
Checked terminals to the maker's torque and recorded loose ones
Checked contacts and overload setting against the motor nameplate
Carried out insulation tests correctly with electronics disconnected, and compared trends
Wrote a clear report with priorities and actions
safety: Only the instructor energises the board and starter; all trainee work is done dead
Do not use compressed air to blow dust into equipment; vacuum it out
Discharge circuits after insulation resistance tests

practical2.title: Install an outdoor lighting control panel with a contactor, time switch and photocell, and write its maintenance schedule
practical2.brief: The assessor gives the group a drawing and a lighting load list for a car park, and the makers' data for an enclosure, a contactor, a time switch and a photocell. The training bay is never connected to a supply during the task. As a group: (1) check that the contactor rating suits the lighting load and that the enclosure's IP rating suits an outdoor coastal site, and record the reasons; (2) mount the enclosure plumb and firm on the training wall, with cable entries from below through correctly sized glands, and fit a lockable isolator; (3) mount the photocell where the drawing shows; (4) wire the panel to the drawing with numbered wires, earth all metal parts and label everything; (5) carry out dead tests (protective conductor continuity, insulation resistance and polarity) and record them; (6) the instructor energises the panel, sets the time switch and checks the photocell and contactor operation while the group watches from a safe distance; and (7) write a handover sheet and a maintenance schedule for the panel, covering tasks, intervals, who does them and what to record. Each member installs or wires at least one part and writes part of the schedule. Photograph each stage and hand in the checks, test record, handover sheet and schedule.
materials: Training wall or bay (not connected to any supply)
